title: Gajakesari yoga: meaning, rules and how common it is | Ask Tota
description: Gajakesari yoga is Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon. The classical rule, why about a third of all charts have it, and what makes one strong or weak.
og_description: Jupiter in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the Moon. Roughly one chart in three has it. Here is what actually separates a strong one from a label.

dek: the elephant and the lion. it is one of the most quoted yogas in vedic astrology and one of the easiest to form: jupiter in a kendra from the moon. the rule is simple, the frequency is high, and the strength conditions are where the real reading is.

llms_desc: the classical definition of Gajakesari yoga (Jupiter in a kendra, the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th, from the Moon), why roughly one in three charts has it, the strength conditions from classical texts, what weakens it, and common myths.

faq.a: a yoga formed when jupiter is in a kendra from the moon, that is in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th sign counted from the moon. the name joins gaja, elephant, and kesari, lion, and the yoga is traditionally linked to reputation, wisdom and lasting good standing.

very common. jupiter can be in any of 12 signs from the moon and 4 of them qualify, so roughly a third of all charts have it on the basic rule. that is why the strength conditions matter more than the label.
no. on the basic definition, about one chart in three has it. a strong gajakesari, with jupiter and the moon both well placed and unafflicted, is much rarer.

faq.q: what are the effects of gajakesari yoga?
faq.a: classical texts describe a person who is respected, intelligent, prosperous and whose reputation lasts. modern astrologers read it as a supportive combination for good judgement and goodwill, with results depending on its strength and the dashas.

jupiter and the moon both dignified, neither combust or debilitated, not afflicted by malefics, ideally aspected by benefics, and the yoga falling in good houses from the lagna. a bright, waxing moon helps.

faq.q: what cancels or weakens gajakesari yoga?
faq.a: a debilitated jupiter in capricorn or moon in scorpio, a combust jupiter, heavy affliction by saturn, rahu or mars, or the combination falling in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna. weak does not mean harmful, just less to deliver.

faq.q: is gajakesari counted from the moon or the lagna?
faq.a: the classical definition counts jupiter's position from the moon. some modern astrologers also look for jupiter in a kendra from the lagna, but that is a different consideration.

faq.q: does jupiter conjunct the moon form gajakesari yoga?
faq.a: yes. the 1st house from the moon is a kendra, so jupiter in the same sign as the moon counts. it is one of the four positions.

faq.q: when does gajakesari yoga give results?
faq.a: traditionally during the dashas and antardashas of jupiter or the moon, and when transits activate them. a yoga describes potential; dashas are read as the timing.

faq.q: is gajakesari yoga a raj yoga?
faq.a: it is often grouped with auspicious yogas and sometimes called raj yoga-like, but strictly it is a chandra yoga, a combination defined from the moon. classical raj yogas involve kendra and trikona lords from the lagna.

faq.q: which classical texts describe gajakesari yoga?
faq.a: it appears in brihat parashara hora shastra and phaladeepika, among others. definitions are consistent on jupiter in a kendra from the moon; texts add strength conditions.

faq.q: can someone without gajakesari yoga be successful?
faq.a: of course. it is one supportive combination among hundreds in vedic astrology, and two thirds of people do not have it. no single yoga decides a life.
